The handbook requires a correct-answer rate of at least eighty percent to pass the knowledge examination. [A01]
The guide describes computer testing in most offices and questions based on its traffic rules, signs, signals and safe-driving material. [A01]
An exact question count and a test duration are not stated in the evidence used here. Those values remain unknown. This preparation uses practice questions; it does not claim an official question bank, a complete examination form or a guaranteed result. First-time applicants should retain the full conditions attached to each rule rather than treat a short study cue as a replacement for the guide.

# Audience and boundaries

This section supports first-time Louisiana passenger-vehicle applicants studying trailer loading, connection, tires and sway. The study scope follows the registered Class E route; the guide also contains other vehicle classes, which are outside this product scope. Learning activities ask the learner to distinguish the person, document or situation covered by a stated rule. Driver licensing decisions, document adjudication and practical driving instruction remain outside these written-knowledge exercises.

sections.markdown:
# Trailer loading, connection, tires and sway

FACT_ID: sec16-F01 | anchor: A01
Before towing a trailer, consult the vehicle manual to confirm that the vehicle has the necessary equipment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F02 | anchor: A01
Towing changes the combined vehicle weight, so allow for its effect on speed choice and stopping room. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F03 | anchor: A01
For a ball-and-coupler hitch, the ball size must fit the coupler to prevent the trailer becoming detached. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F04 | anchor: A01
The hitch must provide an attachment point for safety chains or an approved alternative safety device. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F05 | anchor: A01
Secure the safety connection to the tow vehicle with enough strength to retain the trailer after a hitch separation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F06 | anchor: A01
Cross safety chains beneath the trailer tongue so they can help keep it off the roadway if the main connection fails. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F07 | anchor: A01
Safety chains need enough looseness for sharp turns but must not scrape along the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F08 | anchor: A01
The guide requires a trailer with gross weight of three thousand pounds or more to have brakes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F09 | anchor: A01
The required trailer braking arrangement must allow the towing driver to apply the brakes from the cab. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F10 | anchor: A01
The guide requires the trailer brakes to apply automatically if an accidental separation occurs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F11 | anchor: A01
Trailer lighting includes rear lamps, brake lamps, turn indicators, side-marker lamps and side and rear reflectors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F12 | anchor: A01
The tow vehicle and trailer electrical connectors must be compatible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F13 | anchor: A01
Give the electrical cable enough slack for sharp turns while preventing it from dragging on the ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

FACT_ID: sec16-F14 | anchor: A01
Before towing, test that the trailer’s lamps function properly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0138]

sections.markdown:
# Trailer loading, connection, tires and sway

FACT_ID: sec16-R01 | anchor: A01
Use trailer tires of matching type, size and construction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R02 | anchor: A01
Do not combine radial trailer tires with bias-belted trailer tires. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R03 | anchor: A01
Select trailer tire size, type and load range from its certification label or owner’s manual. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R04 | anchor: A01
A tire’s load rating identifies the weight that tire is designed to carry safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R05 | anchor: A01
Keep trailer tires at the specified pressure and replace tires that are worn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R06 | anchor: A01
The towing vehicle may need a different specified tire pressure for towing, especially with a heavy load. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R07 | anchor: A01
Correct cargo placement improves control of both the tow vehicle and trailer. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R08 | anchor: A01
Use the vehicle and trailer manuals to determine side-to-side load balance and lengthwise cargo distribution. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R09 | anchor: A01
Secure and brace cargo so it cannot move or fall from the trailer during travel. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

FACT_ID: sec16-R10 | anchor: A01
Use the manufacturer’s instructions to set connection height and any weight-distributing hitch equipment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0139]

sections.markdown:
# Accuracy and teaching notes

This section covers the guide’s ordinary trailer safety material rather than the excluded Class D chauffeur chapter. The three-thousand-pound brake threshold and required equipment remain subject to current issuer/legal verification. Use vehicle/trailer manufacturer values for ratings, pressures and hitch setup; no universal pressure increase or equipment capacity is inferred. The source illustration is not treated as evidence for unseen dimensions or connection geometry. [A01] [A02]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “Match the hitch, cross the chains, test the lights, secure the load”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: The coupler connects to a matching hitch ball; the trailer tongue is the forward connection structure. A load rating is a tire capacity rather than a permission to overload the whole vehicle.
Misconception to correct: A secure main hitch makes chains unnecessary, or a tire’s capacity overrides the vehicle’s rating. The guide requires a separate safety connection and manufacturer-based load planning.
